$$
\begin{aligned}{cot}^{2}⁡x & ={csc}^{2}⁡x-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4{cot}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int 4({csc}^{2}⁡x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (4{csc}^{2}⁡x-4)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-4\operatorname{cot}⁡x-4x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. So we can use the identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1+2x+{tan}^{2}⁡x)\text{d}x & =\int (1+{tan}^{2}⁡x+2x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int ({sec}^{2}⁡x+2x)\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡x+{x}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we have to use the identity  $1+{cot}^{2}⁡x={csc}^{2}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}(2+3{x}^{2}+2{cot}^{2}⁡x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}(2(1+{cot}^{2}⁡x)+3{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}(2{csc}^{2}⁡x+3{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =(-2\operatorname{cot}⁡x+{x}^{3}){|}_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-2\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+{(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{3}-[-2\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+{(\frac{\pi }{4})}^{3}] \\  & =-0+\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{8}+2(1)-\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{64} \\  & =2+\frac{7{\pi }^{3}}{64}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Integrating Trigonometric Expressions With Linear Arguments Using the Pythagorean Identities
questions.worked_solution:
From the identity ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1,$ with $\theta =3x+2,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡(3x+2)+{sin}^{2}⁡(3x+2)=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{cos}^{4}⁡(3x+2)+{cos}^{2}⁡(3x+2){sin}^{2}⁡(3x+2)}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡(3x+2)({cos}^{2}⁡(3x+2)+{sin}^{2}⁡(3x+2))}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡(3x+2)}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int {sec}^{2}⁡(3x+2)\,\text{d}x & = \\ \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x+2)+C & .\end{aligned}
$$

Using the identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x,
$$

we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x(1-{tan}^{2}⁡x)}{1-{tan}^{4}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x(1-{tan}^{2}⁡x)}{(1-{tan}^{2}⁡x)(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}{1+{tan}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /6} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
